data.title: A Celtic settlement in 3D
data.excerpt: Our new 3D visualisation presents an idealised impression of a Celtic settlement in the territory of southern Slovakia. Besides larger log buildings the Celts used semi-sunken buildings similar to those later known among the Slavs, and the walls of their daub-plastered houses could be coloured and even carry painted decoration.
data.metaTitle: A Celtic settlement in 3D – southern Slovakia
data.metaDescription: A 3D visualisation of an idealised Celtic settlement in southern Slovakia: log buildings, semi-sunken buildings and houses with painted daub walls.

mediaTexts.alt: A 3D reconstruction of a house with a gabled thatched roof and a gable painted red

children.text: We present to you our new 3D visualisation. This time it is an idealised impression of a Celtic settlement in the territory of southern Slovakia. Besides larger log buildings, the Celts used semi-sunken buildings similar to those we know later among the Slavs, but they were bigger and differed in certain details.

Houses with daub “plaster” could have had coloured walls and even painted decoration. We have also used typical Celtic pottery, weapons and a loom. A walk through a 2,000-year-old Celtic village has an atmosphere all of its own.
For their expert help we thank the archaeologists Radovan Čambal and Branislav Kovár.
